rules.w: Everything that belongs to this user: documents and media (your call), app data in Library (careful), and tool caches that are safe to clear.
Already thrown away, but it keeps using space until the Trash is emptied.
h: Finder > Empty Trash.

rules.t: Git worktrees (Claude Code, going by the folder name)
rules.w: Each folder looks like a separate checked-out copy of a repository. A worktree can hold work that was never committed or merged.
h: In the main repository run `git worktree list`, then `git worktree remove <path>` for the ones you are done with.
Check `git status` inside a worktree before removing it.

rules.w: Downloaded packages kept to speed up installs. npm refills it as needed.
h: `npm cache clean --force`, or delete the folder.

rules.w: Settings, history or data for a command-line or developer tool. Tools often keep both irreplaceable settings and re-creatable caches in the same folder.
h: Zoom in: folders named cache, logs or tmp inside are usually safe to clear.
If you no longer use the tool, the whole folder can usually go.

rules.w: Local AI model files, usually several GB each. They can be downloaded again.
h: `ollama list` shows models and sizes.
`ollama rm <model>` removes one.

rules.w: Installed Rust compilers. Each toolchain is roughly a GB or more.
h: `rustup toolchain list`, then `rustup toolchain uninstall <name>` for ones you do not use.

rules.w: Each version or environment can be hundreds of MB to several GB. Unused ones can be removed and reinstalled later.
h: Remove old versions with the tool that installed them (pyenv, nvm, conda, uv, rustup and so on) rather than deleting folders by hand.

rules.w: Small, and important: keys or credentials that tools use to sign in. Losing them can lock you out of servers or services.
Personal files, often one of a kind. Importance depends on the content and on whether you have a backup or synced copy.
Usually the easiest place to recover space: installers, archives and files you have already used or saved elsewhere. Skim before deleting, because some things only exist here.
h: Sort by size or date. Old .dmg, .pkg and .zip files are the typical safe wins.

rules.w: Photos you took are irreplaceable unless backed up or in a cloud library. Screenshots and downloaded images usually matter less.
Once the software is installed, the installer is no longer needed and can normally be downloaded again. Exception: installers for paid or discontinued software you could not get again.
h: Check the app is installed and working, then delete.

rules.w: If you have already extracted it, the contents probably exist twice. If the archive is itself a backup or export, it may be the only copy.
h: Check whether an extracted folder with the same name sits next to it.

rules.w: Mostly data and settings that apps rely on, mixed with parts that are safe to clear such as Caches, Logs and Xcode DerivedData.
Each folder belongs to one app and holds its data: projects, databases, downloaded content, sometimes caches.
h: Look for folders of apps you have uninstalled; those leftovers are usually safe to remove.
For apps you use, free space from inside the app.

rules.w: A cache inside an app's data folder. The app rebuilds it when needed.
h: Quit the app first, then delete the contents.

rules.w: Device backups made through Finder. Each can be tens of GB. If one is the only backup of a device, it is irreplaceable.
h: Delete old backups through Finder: select the device, then Manage Backups.
Check the device also backs up to iCloud before removing its last local backup.

rules.w: Holds an app's data. Deleting it loses that data or resets the app.
h: Free space from inside the app that owns it.

rules.w: Apps rebuild caches when they need them. Clearing costs some re-downloading and slower first launches, not data.
h: Quit the app first, then delete that app's folder inside Caches.
Some caches are large on purpose (downloaded browsers for test tools, package downloads) and will simply download again.

rules.w: Downloaded packages kept in case you reinstall.
h: `brew cleanup -s` clears it.

rules.w: Browser builds downloaded by Playwright for automated testing.
h: Safe to delete. `npx playwright install` downloads them again when a project needs them.

rules.w: Each folder is one app's private data: documents, databases and caches. Deleting a folder resets that app.
h: Free space from inside the app (clear downloads or offline content).
Folders of apps you have uninstalled are usually safe to remove.

rules.w: Holds Docker's virtual disk (Docker.raw) with every image, container and volume. Deleting the file wipes all of them.
h: `docker system df` shows what is using the space.
`docker system prune` removes stopped containers and dangling images. Adding `-a` removes all unused images; adding `--volumes` also deletes unused volumes and their data.
Docker Desktop's Resources settings let you lower the disk image size limit.

rules.w: Build output, simulators and device support files. Several parts are safe to clear; zoom in.
Each simulated device has its own disk with installed apps and data.
h: `xcrun simctl delete unavailable` removes simulators whose runtime is gone.
`xcrun simctl erase all` wipes the data in every simulator but keeps the devices.

rules.w: Xcode recreates this on the next build. The cost is one slow rebuild per project.
h: Quit Xcode, then delete the contents.

rules.w: Deleting these loses saved passwords, keys and certificates.
These files sync with iCloud. Deleting one here deletes it from iCloud and from your other devices too.
h: To free space but keep the file in iCloud, right-click it in Finder and choose Remove Download.

rules.w: Often the largest personal files. Camera originals and finished exports are irreplaceable unless backed up. Render caches, proxies and screen recordings usually are not.
h: Moving finished projects and raw footage to external or network storage frees the most space.

rules.t: Video render cache or generated media (likely)
rules.w: The folder name matches what video editors such as DaVinci Resolve use for render cache, proxy or optimized media. These are generated from your source footage and can be rebuilt, at the cost of render time.
h: In DaVinci Resolve, Playback > Delete Render Cache removes cache safely.
Make sure the folder holds only generated files, not your originals.

rules.w: Large by nature. Camera originals and finished exports are irreplaceable unless backed up; screen recordings and downloaded videos usually are not.
h: Move footage you want to keep to external or network storage.

rules.w: Photos are usually irreplaceable unless they are backed up or in a cloud library.
h: Make sure a backup exists before deleting originals.

rules.w: Your photo collection in a single package. Deleting pieces from inside it corrupts the library.
h: Delete photos inside the Photos app, then empty Recently Deleted.
With iCloud Photos on, the Optimize Mac Storage setting in Photos keeps smaller versions locally.
The whole library can be moved to an external drive.

rules.w: This is in your home folder, with no more specific rule. Treat it as personal data: how important it is depends on what it is and whether you have another copy.
h: Check that anything you cannot recreate is backed up before deleting it.

rules.w: Everything committed in this repository. If it is fully pushed to a remote you could clone it again; anything unpushed (commits, branches, stashes) exists only here.
h: `git gc --prune=now` can shrink it without losing history.
Before deleting a repository, check `git status` and `git log --branches --not --remotes`.

rules.w: Fully re-creatable from the project's package.json and lockfile.
h: Restore later with the project's install command (npm, pnpm, yarn or bun install).
Old projects you are not working on are the best candidates.

rules.w: Compiled output for the project next to it. Rebuilt on the next build.
h: `cargo clean` (Rust) or `mvn clean` (Maven), or delete the folder.
